name: btor2-sim
notes: The naive first citizen (KERNEL.md §8): explicit-state search on the bit-vector fragment — exhaustive breadth-first with fixpoint detection when the free-input space is small (<=16 bits at frame 0, <=12 per later frame), yielding witnesses or all(k)/all(inf); deterministic guided sampling otherwise (witnesses only). Effort derives from the wall argument, never the clock. Sampling partials report the number of failed trials, which is the ledger's free lower bound on witness surprisal (KERNEL.md §5). Era-6 revision 1 = the Era-5 btor2-sim text re-cut, plus graceful refusal of array programs. Revision 2 evaluates sdiv/srem/smod (four hwmcc24-mini programs crashed the first revision on srem) and refuses every remaining unsupported op with a partial, and adds ledger.py (KERNEL.md §5): the same solver byte for byte, now reporting the failed-trial surprisal bound and the cleared bits beside every path. Revision 3 scales the effort by model size: the enumeration and sampling budgets derive from the wall argument divided by the node count in units of 2000 nodes (unchanged for models up to 2000 nodes, so the predecessor corpus is byte-identical), because a 40-frame sample of a 5000-node machine costs 100x a small one and the first revision's fixed budgets ran past twice the wall on translated C programs. Revision 4 adds arrays, on array programs only: the bit-vector path is revision 3's text byte for byte, so the predecessor corpus is byte-identical. An array program takes a second path at the end of solve.py — btor2@5's front end embedded (lineage btor2-interp-g1); arrays carried as sparse maps whose cells are drawn the first time they are read and remembered, so the sampled run is consistent with the stimulus it emits ({"default": v, "set": {index: value}} per free array node per frame, exactly what the interpreter reads; a cell never written before it is read holds the default, as in the interpreter); every candidate witness replayed through the embedded interpreter before it is written. Sampling only — witnesses, never a claim — and guided: at every frame one case of every constraint, of the next function of every one-bit state that bad depends on monotonically, and of bad itself is drawn at random, cases whose state-only guards already fail are pruned, and the equalities free = expr and the one-bit literals in the chosen case fix the free nodes they name; the rest are drawn as before, and three attempts in four are guided. That reaches the machines whose transition relation is written as equalities over next-value inputs (the sosylab encodings of hwmcc24-arrays), which uniform draws never hit. The budget is a count of node evaluations per wall second, from the wall argument, never the clock.
